description: An old, weathered hand holds a brass stylus over a large parchment portolan-style chart covered in red and blue rhumb lines, with a compass rose and a small figure on a camel near a coastline at right. Shell dishes of red, blue and yellow pigment and a jar of brushes sit at left, in a dim timber-beamed stone workshop. No letters, border or frame, nothing graphic.
reason: Shows a cartographer's hand drawing rhumb lines on a medieval sea chart with pigments and a camel rider, but the card is the 1381 killing of Wat Tyler at Smithfield. Nothing of the parley, the king, the peasants or the London setting appears; repaint it as the confrontation at Smithfield.
